Kabc020074812023 
Before The Court Of I Addl. Small Causes Judge & Acjm &
 Motor Vehicles Accident Claim Tribunal, Bengaluru . 
 (Scch-11)
 Dated This The 05Th Day Of December - 2024 
 Present: Sri.Narendra.B.R., B.Sc, L.L.B.
 I Addl.Small Causes Judge & Acjm
 & Member - Mact
 Mvc No.1650/2023
PETITIONER:
 Kum.Harshithanand,
 D/o.H.R.Ramanand,
 Aged about 19 years,
 R/at No.52, Vatsalya,
 Residency, 9th Cross, 2nd Main,
 Byrappa Garden, 3rd Stage,
 Basaveshwaranagar,
 Bengaluru - 560085.
 (By Sri.T.K.Shanthappa, Adv.) 
 //Versus//
RESPONDENTS: 
 1. Sri.Amithanand.R.,
 S/o.Ramanand,
 R/at No.52, Vatsalya,
 Residency, 9th Cross, 2nd Main,
 SCCH-11 2 MVC.No.1650/2023  Byrappa Garden, 3rd Stage,
 Basaveshwaranagar,
 Bengaluru - 560085.
 (Owner of the Mahindra Mojo  vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JU-0190). 
 2. The Manager,
 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.,
 Ltd., Off/at No.1/2, 4th Floor,
 Golden Heights, 4th M Block,

 Bengaluru - 560010.

1  (Policy No.OG-23-1701-1802-00169791  Valid from 14.07.2022 to 16.07.2023.
 (Resp.1 - Exparte) 
 (Resp.2 - By Sri.Gururaj Salur, Adv.)
 J U D G M E N T This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 19.02.2023 at about 04.15 p.m., the petitioner was travelling in a Two Wheeler bearing Regn.No.KA- 02-JU-0190 as a pillion rider and when she reached near Sangabasavanadoodi, BM Road, Kasaba Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk and District, the rider of the said vehicle drove at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against pedestrian. As a result, petitioner lost balance and fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Ramakrishna Hospital and then shifted to KIMS Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .4,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges. 
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was a Student and doing Tailoring as a part time Work and earning .20,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability. The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider. The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 
3. In pursuance of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte. The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement. 
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically. The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident. Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed. Respondent No.2 admitted the aspect of issue of policy of insurance pertaining to the offending vehicle and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy. Further contended that on the date of alleged accident the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license. Further contended that this is a self-accident case, the petitioner himself was riding the motor cycle and fallen from the same. Further at the time of accident, the petitioner was not wearing safety headgear. The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. Hence,
prayed for dismissal of petition. 
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
2 1. Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.02.2013 at about 04.15 p.m., Sangabasavanadoddi, BM Road, Kasaba Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk and District, while she was proceeding on a Mahindra Mojo Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JU-0190 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent riding of above said vehicle by its rider? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner got examined as PW.1 and Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed her side evidence. The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary. 
7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 19.02.2023 at about 04.15 p.m., near Sangabasavanadoddi, BM Road, Kasaba Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk and District, while she was proceeding on a Mahindra Mojo Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JU-0190 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent riding of above said vehicle by its rider, accident was caused in which she sustained grievous injuries. 
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JU-0190 by its driver, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1. In the chief examination, she deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider, the accident occurred. On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner. Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination. 
11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of motorcycle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by one Hanumanthaiah, with police on Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/ 
3 19.02.2023 . On the basis of first information lodged by son of petitioner, the police registered a case as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC. In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle. The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle. The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3. The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents. In the mahazar also,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle. Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned. The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident. The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle. The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident. The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC. In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle. The police filed the final report after detailed investigation. The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation. No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner. The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police. In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner. The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle. PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited. No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident. 
12. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner. In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence. The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident. The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner. On perusal of entire record, the rider of insured vehicle, driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner. Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P7,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JU-0190 by its rider and same resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner. Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative. 
13. Issue No.2: In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation. In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
4 medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment. In order to prove the injuries sustained by the petitioner, she has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6, wherein it discloses that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature. So,
on perusal of records, the petitioner appears to have taken treatment in hospital as an inpatient and she has produced Ex.P8 - Discharge Summary issued by KIMS Hospital and Research Center and also got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.2 through whom Ex.P.12 and P.13 documents are got marked. PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent and opined that the petitioner is having physical disability of right lower limb at 42% and to the whole body at 14%. By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering. 
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses: The petitioner claimed compensation towards medical expenses. 
The petitioner contended that she took treatment at the Hospital. In order to substantiate the said aspect, the petitioner produced 97 medical bills totally amounting to Rs.1,49,768/-. On perusal of bills furnished by petitioner, it contains medical bills pertaining to Amitanand also. The bills furnished by petitioner do not pertain to petitioner alone and it discloses the name of respondent No.1 also, who appears to have taken treatment. The medical bills numbered as 6, 9, 12 to 14, 16 to 21, 28, 29, 42 to 45, 49 to 51, 53, 55, 57 to 59, 62, 64, 65, 67, 70 to 72, 74, 76, 78, 79, 82 to 87, 89, 91,
92 and 94 to 96 do not disclose the name of petitioner and they do not appear to be pertaining to the petitioner. The said medical bills do not pertain to the petitioner. The total amount of said bills is Rs.40,307/- and said amount cannot be considered to be expenses incurred by petitioner. As the above mentioned bills do not pertain to the petitioner, same is not taken for consideration. The medical bills furnished by petitioner disclose that a sum of Rs.1,09,461/- is incurred by her towards the medical expenses. The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence. No satisfactory materials to rebut or disprove the medical bills, are being placed before the Tribunal. 
The petitioner not entitled to the amount mentioned in the medical bills furnished by her as the same appear to include the bills pertaining to Amithanand also. So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,09,461/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses. 
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges: On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 19.02.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital. 
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as she sustained injuries. So, during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment. The petitioner produced Ex.P.8 - Discharge Summary issued by KIMS Hospital & Research Centre, wherein petitioner shown to have taken treatment as an inpatient from 19.02.2023 to 03.03.2023 i.e., for a period of 14 days. Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 14 days to a sum of .7,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant. 
Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
5 (iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Vatsalya Residency, Byrappa Garden,
Basaveshwaranagar, Bengaluru, she has admitted to hospital for treatment. In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.8. Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges. 
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment: 
The petitioner contended that she was a Student and also doing Tailoring as a Part Time Work and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month. In order to prove her income as per her contention, the petitioner not produced any document. The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that she was doing tailoring and earning .20,000/- per month. Though the petitioner contended that she was doing tailoring, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate the said contention. In the absence of satisfactory materials,
notional income is to be taken into consideration. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-. On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended her work for some time due to accidental injuries. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- towards loss of income during treatment. 
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity: 
The petitioner contended that due to accident, she was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement. The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center,
Bengaluru, as PW.2. PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities. The doctor deposed that petitioner sustained fracture of right distal 1/3rd leg both bones and underwent CRIF with IMIL Nailing for right tibia and ORIF with Plate and screws for the right distal fibula later discharged. The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to right lower limb at 42% and to the whole body at 14%. In order to prove the disability,
doctor has produced Ex.P.12 & 13 i.e., Clinical Note and X-ray film. PW.2 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.2 and in the cross examination the witness stated that there is no difficulties for the studies of petitioner and also no complications at the fractures site. PW.2 also stated that the petitioner can walk independently and there is no severe loss of movement at the joints. PW.2 also stated that the petitioner can perform day to day activities but with difficulty. The witness not deposed that the petitioner might not be able to do her daily activities and also not deposed about difficulty in continuing her studies or to her work. The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner is able to do her daily activities subject to some difficulties. 
Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
6 On consideration of oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do her work with difficulty. As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%. 
In order to prove age of the petitioner, she has produced Ex.P.11 - Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth is mentioned as 06.10.2004. As per the document furnished by petitioner, her age appears to be 19 years at the time of accident. The respondents not furnished any materials to doubt or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to her age. No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to doubt or disprove the age of petitioner. The accident occurred on 19.02.2023. As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 19 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier. As per Smt.Sarla Verma case '18' multiplier is applicable. 
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income. Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
 Loss of future earning p.a. (10% of prior annual  income) = .19,200/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 18 Loss of future earnings - (.19,200/- x 18) = .3,45,600/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .3,45,600/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she can perform her activities but with some difficulties. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities. 
(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.2 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and the estimate cost for the surgery is around .60,000/-. The petitioner or PW.2 not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that .60,000/- is required for Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
7 the surgery. Though PW.2 stated the estimate cost of surgery to be .60,000/-, the same is not substantiated by any cogent and satisfactory materials. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .30,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses. 
14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl . No . Particulars Amount  a. Towards injury pain and .50,000/-
 suffering  b. Towards Medical Expenses .1,09,461/-
 c. Towards food and extra .7,000/-
 nourishment and medical  attendant  d. Towards conveyance .10,000/-
 e. Towards loss of income .30,000/-
 during treatment  f. Towards loss of future .3,45,600/-
 earning  g. Deprivation of future .10,000/-
 amenities  h. Towards future medical .30,000/-
 expenses  Total compensation .5,92,061/-
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of .5,92,061/-.
15. In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law. Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908. Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded." 
In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2. It is already held that the Harshithanand vs Amithanand.R on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101301651/
8 accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Mahindra Mojo Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA- 02-JU-0190. Respondent No.2 not disputed the aspect of issue of policy pertaining to the offending vehicle. As per the materials on record, the policy of insurance appears to be valid and existing as on the date of accident. So, respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative. 
17. Issue No.3: In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost. 
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .5,92,061/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand Sixty One only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization. (future medical expenses shall not carry any interest) 
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner. Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award. 
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60%
shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019. 
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to her account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court. The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-. Draw up award accordingly.
